raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Dense mono decode for Qwen3.8-27B on 128-CU gfx950 (MI350P). **Stacked on #61573**, which adds the dense mono decode
for MI355X; the first two commits are #61573's and the rest are this PR's. Review the later commits. Draft until
#61573 lands.

AI assistance was used in developing this PR (code, tests, measurements and this description).

## Claims

- The K1 (GDN mixer) and K2 (MXFP4 FFN) persistent kernels of #61573 build and run with the grid width taken from the
  device's CU count: 256 (MI355X, MI350X) or 128 (MI350P). Other counts are refused with a message; #61573 refuses
  everything below 256 CUs.
- 256-CU builds are unchanged apart from one numerics fix: of the 80 K1 / K2 configurations, the 32 K2 compile to
  byte-identical code objects (sha256) with and without this PR, and the 48 K1 differ only by keeping beta in fp32
  (last bullet); with that line reverted all 80 are identical to #61573's.
- On MI350P (TP1, MTP off, same image, flag on vs off, default row caps): output throughput +19.1 % at one request
  (8k / 1k, TPOT 9.21 → 7.67 ms), +14.8 % at two, +12.0 % at four, +0.5 % at eight. Above the caps nothing changes.
- With MTP-3 (TP1), mono now runs the verify steps (until now the flag refused speculative decoding): K1 takes each
  request's 1 + 3 tokens through the conv and the recurrence in order, as vLLM's spec-decode kernels do, and K2 the
  rows. Output throughput +19.9 / +18.7 % at one request (two prompt seeds, TPOT 3.98 → 3.29 ms), +3.7 % at two
  (a verify step of two requests is 8 rows, above the default caps of 4), unchanged at four and eight. On a recent
  nightly whose stock MXFP4 decode GEMM is AITER's FlyDSL A4W4 kernel, one request gains about 6 % (verify step
  9.67 → 7.88 ms).
- Accuracy on MI350P is unchanged within run-to-run noise: GSM8K in the model card's setting (paired over three
  seeds, −0.18 ± 0.36 pt thinking, −0.45 ± 0.45 pt non-thinking), GSM8K chat, GPQA Diamond, RULER NIAH 64k / 128k;
  with MTP-3 at one request (K1 and K2 on every verify step), GSM8K card setting +0.53 ± 0.67 pt thinking,
  −0.68 ± 0.80 pt non-thinking.
- K1 and K2 are bit-exact on MI350P with the stock paths #61573's tests and startup checks compare against: K2 with
  the Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4` (TP1 S 1-8, TP2 S 1-16), K1 with the stock GDN decode (TP1 S 1-8; TP2 S 1-16 without
  out_proj; with out_proj see Details) and, on MTP-3 verify steps of one and two requests, with the spec-decode
  path vLLM serves: `causal_conv1d_update` with either the sigmoid-gated delta rule kernel + RMSNormGated (this
  base) or main's fused MTP decode kernel (#61855; checked on a recent nightly). A server that runs the MXFP4 linears on the AITER ASM GEMM (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`, as
  here) accumulates differently, so mono's greedy outputs are not byte-identical to that server's; accuracy is
  compared statistically.
- Fixes that apply to #61573 independently of the CU count: K2 follows the installed AITER's split-K (the bit-exact
  startup check failed with current AITER); the mono graph no longer takes over Model Runner V2's piecewise-cudagraph
  capture (the engine died on the first prefill); the GDN state-slot mapping runs once a step instead of in every GDN
  layer (144 launches a step); a GDN layer above K1's row cap no longer hands out_proj's output to K2 in place of its
  input (the skip hook was never installed); K1 rounded beta to bf16, which the stock decode kernel stopped doing
  in #53877 (K1's strict test failed by one bf16 ulp in ≈ 4 % of the outputs).

## Validation

Hardware: 1x MI350P (gfx950, 128 CUs, 4 XCDs), TP1, `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`. Image: vLLM v0.32.0 + AITER
main (2026-10-30) with the MI350P enablement PRs, FlyDSL 0.4.1, Triton 3.8.0 (`669b31ac`), and this branch's `vllm/`
Python files overlaid at a commit of this branch (`739f2c1d3e` for the tables without MTP, `1a10d1925f` for MTP;
the later commits make K1's spec l2 norm bit-exact). Mono arm: that image with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`; control arm: the same image with the flag
unset, except where a table says otherwise.

### Performance (`sglang.bench_serving`, random, range ratio 0.8)

Decode-bound cases, MTP off, both arms in the same image (control: flag unset):

| In / out | Conc | Out tok/s off → on (default caps 4) | Δ | TPOT p50 ms off → on | Out tok/s, caps 8 |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| 8192 / 1024 | 1 (seed 21) | 104.6 → 124.6 | +19.1 % | 9.21 → 7.67 | 124.3 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 1 (seed 22) | 105.0 → 125.0 | +19.1 % | 9.20 → 7.67 | 124.9 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 2 | 196.4 → 225.5 | +14.8 % | 9.83 → 8.52 | 224.7 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 344.3 → 385.6 | +12.0 % | 11.05 → 9.84 | 384.1 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 8 | 571.8 → 574.6 | +0.5 % | 13.19 → 13.19 | 579.1 (+1.3 %) |

With MTP-3 (`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`), branch at `1a10d1925f`, flag unset vs
set; K1 and K2 run the verify steps (a request's verify step is 4 rows):

| In / out | Conc | Out tok/s MTP-3 → + mono (default caps 4) | Δ | TPOT p50 ms | Out tok/s, caps 8 | Δ |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| 8192 / 1024 | 1 (seed 21) | 223.7 → 268.2 | +19.9 % | 3.98 → 3.29 | 267.0 | +19.4 % |
| 8192 / 1024 | 1 (seed 22) | 222.7 → 264.3 | +18.7 % | 3.76 → 3.19 | 266.7 | +19.7 % |
| 8192 / 1024 | 2 | 353.3 → 366.4 | +3.7 % | 5.22 → 5.10 | 389.4 | +10.2 % |
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 592.7 → 592.1 | −0.1 % | 5.97 → 5.98 | 591.1 | −0.3 % |
| 8192 / 1024 | 8 | 930.4 → 932.9 | +0.3 % | 7.67 → 7.65 | 934.1 | +0.4 % |

Prompts: 8 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 at concurrency 1 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 8, warmup = concurrency. One run per cell. Without MTP
the two concurrency-1 seeds agree within 0.4 %, and controls on different images (identical outside mono) within
1.5 % (`739f2c1d3e` vs `1a10d1925f`, flag unset, MTP off: 104.6 / 105.0 vs 103.0 / 104.7 at one request). With caps 4
a verify step of two requests (8 rows) runs stock; caps 8 run it through K1 + K2, +10.2 % here, where the stock MXFP4
linears are the AITER ASM GEMM. On a recent nightly (vLLM main, same MI350P, MTP-3) whose stock decode GEMM is AITER's
FlyDSL A4W4 kernel, the same 8-row steps ran about 5 % slower than stock (412.6 / 407.4 vs 432.8 / 433.4 tok/s at
two requests; caps 4: 431.8), so the default caps stay 4 with speculative decoding; one request there: verify step
9.67 → 7.88 ms, 4k / 1k output throughput +6.5 %, four and more requests within −1 … +3 %. With K2 alone on the verify steps (an earlier commit, K1 off)
the gain at one request was +4.9 % and none at two. TTFT is unchanged (prefill takes the stock path).

Wider and prefill-bound cases (control: the base image; mono does not run above 8 rows):

| In / out | Conc | Out tok/s off → on | Δ | TPOT p50 ms off → on |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| 8192 / 1024 | 16 | 878.8 → 883.6 | +0.5 % | 17.21 → 17.10 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 32 | 1181.9 → 1188.0 | +0.5 % | 25.25 → 25.13 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 64 | 1471.7 → 1477.2 | +0.4 % | 40.66 → 40.44 |
| 128000 / 1024 | 4 | 82.7 → 84.0 | +1.6 % | 37.95 → 37.19 |
| 128000 / 1024 | 8 | 92.6 → 92.5 | −0.1 % | 73.13 → 73.25 |

96 / 128 / 256 prompts at concurrency 16 / 32 / 64, 32 / 64 at 128k; an earlier build of this branch (`d6ede56f1a`,
row caps 8) vs the base image without this branch.

Per launch on MI350P (CUDA-graph replay, real shapes): K2 67 / 70 / 79 µs and K1 27.6 / 40.5 / 58 µs at 1 / 4 / 8
rows.
At 8 rows a torch-profiler trace shows K1 + K2 taking about as long as the stock kernels they replace (the MI350P
MXFP4 ASM GEMMs run gate_up at M = 8 in 34 µs, about the bandwidth K2's GEMM phases reach); at 1-4 rows mono saves
the per-kernel launch and activation-quantization overhead of the stock path. #61573 reports larger gains on
MI355X (+34 % at concurrency 4), where the stock path is further from its bandwidth bound.

### Accuracy

MTP off, row caps 8, branch at `0846b5d5a2`. The later commits change K1's decode outputs only by moving
them onto the stock path's bits (fp32 beta, the gated norm's reduction order; at most one bf16 ulp in ≈ 4 % of the
outputs before) and leave K2's unchanged (the state-slot mapping is the same indices; the per-CTA norm gives a
bit-identical x, checked: in_proj_qkvz bit-exact with the stock GEMM), so these results stand for the head. At 8 concurrent requests the decode steps stay inside the
caps, so K1 and K2 produce nearly every generated token; at 16 and 32 they mostly do not, so those rows check the
flag-on server rather than the kernels.

| Eval | Concurrency | non-mono | mono |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot, chat template, thinking off, greedy, 250 questions, flexible / strict | 8 | 0.920 / 0.916 | 0.932 / 0.916 |
| GPQA Diamond, thinking on, greedy, max 32k tokens, 198 questions | 8 | 0.773 | 0.768 |
| RULER `niah_single_2` 64k, 50 samples | 8 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| RULER `niah_single_2` 128k, 50 samples | 8 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| GSM8K 5-shot, chat template, thinking off, greedy, 250 questions, flexible / strict | 32 | 0.920 / 0.912 | 0.920 / 0.916 |
| GPQA Diamond, thinking on, greedy, max 32k tokens, 198 questions | 16 | 0.778 | 0.778 |

GPQA's standard error at 198 questions is about 0.03 (the 0.005 difference is one question); GSM8K's at 250 about
0.017. One run per cell.

GSM8K in the model card's setting (`lm_eval` `local-completions`, 5-shot, full 1319 questions, sampled; thinking:
task `gsm8k`, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, max_gen_toks 3072; non-thinking: the card's `gsm8k_nothink`
task, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, presence_penalty 1.5; card: 94.996 / 89.92 flexible), 8 concurrent, both arms on
the same image, three repeats per arm with request seeds 2004-2006 (the same seed in both arms of a repeat):

| Mode | non-mono, flexible-extract | mono, flexible-extract | mono − non-mono, paired |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Thinking | 0.9356 / 0.9272 / 0.9371 (mean 0.9333) | 0.9318 / 0.9295 / 0.9333 (mean 0.9315) | −0.18 ± 0.36 pt |
| Non-thinking | 0.8969 / 0.8961 / 0.9030 (mean 0.8987) | 0.8954 / 0.8908 / 0.8961 (mean 0.8941) | −0.45 ± 0.45 pt |

(± is one standard error of the per-question paired difference over the 3 × 1319 question runs.) Three earlier
repeats per arm all sent lm-eval's default request seed (1234), so they differ only through batch-dependent numerics
and are not independent draws; they give thinking 0.940 / 0.948 / 0.948 vs 0.939 / 0.935 / 0.931 and non-thinking
0.901 / 0.893 / 0.904 vs 0.912 / 0.895 / 0.907. Over all six runs per arm: thinking 0.939 vs 0.933, non-thinking
0.899 vs 0.899.

With MTP-3, one request at a time (a verify step of one request is 4 rows, inside the cap), the same request seed
(2004) in both arms; branch at `f70f45a7c4` (K1 and K2 on the verify steps), and for comparison `739f2c1d3e` (K2
only, K1 off):

| Mode | MTP-3, flexible / strict | MTP-3 + mono, flexible / strict | mono − MTP-3, paired (flexible) | Eval wall time |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Thinking, K1 + K2 | 0.9265 / 0.9227 | 0.9318 / 0.9333 | +0.53 ± 0.67 pt | 23:45 → 18:38 |
| Non-thinking, K1 + K2 | 0.8961 / 0.8969 | 0.8893 / 0.8878 | −0.68 ± 0.80 pt | 14:12 → 11:55 |
| Thinking, K2 only | 0.9265 / 0.9227 | 0.9303 / 0.9356 | +0.38 ± 0.69 pt | 23:15 → 22:27 |
| Non-thinking, K2 only | 0.8961 / 0.8969 | 0.8908 / 0.8908 | −0.53 ± 0.76 pt | 14:09 → 13:33 |

(The MTP-3 arm is the same server in both pairs; its two runs gave identical scores.)

`lm_eval` (`local-chat-completions` for GSM8K chat and NIAH, `local-completions` for the card-setting GSM8K) and
`sglang.test.run_eval` (GPQA) against the servers.

### Compile-only, no GPU (FlyDSL 0.4.1, `COMPILE_ONLY=1 ARCH=gfx950`)

80 configurations (TP1 K2 S 1-8 with and without `oproj`; TP1 K1 S 1-8, first layer and not; TP2 K2 S 1-16; TP2
K1 S 1-16 with and without `out_proj`), each for #61573, this PR at 256 CTAs and this PR at 128 CTAs: all compile;
the 256-CTA code objects are identical to #61573's except K1's fp32 beta (identical with it reverted); no VGPR spills
or scratch at either width (max 247 VGPRs at 128 CTAs, K1 TP1 at 8 rows; TP2 K1 has SGPR spills to VGPR lanes, as
in #61573). The K1 verify-step builds (`spec=4`, S 4 and 8, first layer and not) compile at both widths with no
spills (max 218 VGPRs), and the spec changes leave all 160 non-spec code objects unchanged.

## Details

**Why #61573 does not run on 128 CUs.** K1 and K2 run one CTA per CU, all co-resident, exchanging data through
spin-waited mailboxes, so the grid must equal the CU count; #61573 hard-codes 256 and refuses smaller GPUs (a
256-CTA grid would deadlock on 128 CUs). Several stage layouts also assume 256: one o_proj owner per CTA for 160
owners, one whole down row group per CTA (320 = 256 + 64 split), 4 in_proj_qkvz groups per CTA filling the 8 waves,
and the flag / scratch regions sized by 256.

**What changed.**
- `mono/tiling.py` (new, pure Python): `resolve_grid(cus, override)` picks the width (256, 128; else `ValueError`
  naming the validated widths); `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_GRID` may select a validated width at most the CU
  count (to run the 128-CTA build on a 256-CU GPU). The FFN / GDN geometries move here with the grid as a field,
  plus the per-stage pass plans and their invariants (checked at import for both widths).
- K1 / K2 (`dense_gdn.py`, `dense_ffn.py`): the grid is a field of the build key (so it is in FlyDSL's JIT key; the
  128-CTA kernel symbols end in `_g128`). Stages whose tasks outnumber the CTAs take more passes per CTA, each task
  computed exactly as before: o_proj / out_proj / K1 front owners `bid + p * grid` (a second pass on CTAs 0..31 at
  128); in_proj_qkvz in passes of 4 groups; down's whole row groups and its split group in tile passes; gate_up 8
  whole groups and 8 columns of a split one per CTA; GDN tasks in one pass at TP1 (up to 48 tasks) and in passes of
  whole tokens at TP2 above 24 (a token's tasks all run in the same pass, so no CTA waits on a later pass). At 256
  every stage is one pass and the traced program is unchanged (offsets of 0 emit nothing; the down store keeps its
  original form).
- `dense_mono.py`: refuses with the resolver's message instead of `< 256`; passes the grid to both build keys; a
  build wider than the device's CUs raises instead of hanging.
- K2 split-K: K2 is bit-exact with the stock Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4` only if it splits K the same way. #61573
  hard-codes 4 / 4 / 2 splits; AITER's current `get_splitk` gives gate_up 2, down 2 at TP1 and 1 at TP2 (not
  CU-dependent), so #61573's startup self-check refuses to start with current AITER. K2 probes the stock split
  counts once per width at startup and builds them (`FfnBuild.gu_split / d_split / o_split`; 0 keeps the default).
  Without the probe `DenseFfnTest::test_bit_exact` fails on this stack; `StockSplitTest` checks the probe against
  AITER's `get_splitk`. The probe runs once in model preparation, so there is no new host synchronization in
  steady-state decode.
- Model Runner V2: its PIECEWISE cudagraphs for the stock model are captured by dummy steps that look like pure
  decode; #61573's mono graph took them over, the stock piecewise graphs for widths up to the cap were never
  captured, and the first prefill of such a width tried to capture at run time on the default stream
  (`CUDA graphs must be captured on a non-default stream`). The mono graph now skips PIECEWISE runtime-mode steps;
  pure decode runs under FULL cudagraphs and still takes it. Reproducer: the serve command below with the flag on
  and any request; before the fix the engine dies on its first prefill, after it the smoke requests, the benchmarks
  and the evals above run. Not covered by a unit test (it needs a capturing engine).
- K1 front on 128 CTAs (up to 4 rows): every CTA runs the input norm on the whole rows itself with K2's
  `run_norm`, which reduces in the owners' order, in place of 160 owner tasks (a second pass on CTAs 0..31) and two
  grid-wide hand-offs. x is bit-identical; K1 27.6 / 32.3 / 40.5 µs at 1 / 2 / 4 rows (was 30.3 / 35.1 / 43.5).
  Wider steps keep the owners (the kept rows spill there). 256-CTA builds keep the owners.
- GDN state slots: the copy + null-slot mapping of the state indices ran in every GDN layer (3 launches x 48); GDN
  layers of a KV-cache group share the indices, so it runs once per group a step. −0.5 ms of GPU time a step at one
  request.
- Speculative decoding (TP1): `K1Build.spec` = tokens a request in a verify step (1 + k). A GDN task becomes a
  request's tokens in order: the conv slides its window from offset `n_acc - 1` and rewrites the widened conv state
  (slot `idx[r, 0]`, length 2 + spec), the recurrence starts from slot `idx[r, n_acc - 1]` and stores each token's
  state to `idx[r, j]`, null slots (≤ 0) are skipped — the semantics of
  `causal_conv1d_update(num_accepted_tokens=…)` and `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update(ssm_state_indices=[R,
  1 + k])`. The spec kernel holds one q / k element a lane over two waves, so on spec builds K1's l2 norm reduces each
  wave and adds the two sums (bit-exact; with the decode kernel's order the core differed by one bf16 ulp in a few
  elements a step). The accepted counts ride in the `w_os` argument (unused without out_proj), so the kernel ABI and
  the non-spec code objects are unchanged. `dense_mono.py` reads vLLM's persistent spec buffers and enters only whole
  verify steps (requests x (1 + k) == rows, from tensor shapes, no host sync); partial verify steps and warm-up
  batches run stock. A startup self-check runs K1 on verify steps against the stock spec kernels and an fp32
  reference. Where the GDN layers serve verify steps with the fused MTP decode kernel
  (`enable_fused_gdn_spec_decode`; main since #61855), `K1Build.spec_fused` takes its numerics: launched, it keeps the
  decode kernel's state layout, so the recurrence is unchanged, but its q / k l2 norm sums each of two warps with
  the first DPP step contracted into an fma, and its gated norm sums the squares in tiles of 32 rows (rows 16 apart
  contracted, then xor 8 … 1; tiles added (t0 + t2) + (t1 + t3)); the self-check then compares against that kernel.
  The default caps (4) take a verify step of one MTP-3 request. With K1 switched off, each GDN layer is the compiled stock layer up to out_proj's input (a shallow
  view with out_proj as passthrough, so inductor fuses it as in the stock graph) and K2 takes the rows. TP2 still
  refuses speculative decoding.
- Tests: `test_amd_dense_mono_tiling.py` (new, CPU only, wired into the existing Buildkite job) replays every
  stage's task placement at both widths (each task exactly once; GDN passes closed under their hand-offs) and checks
  the grid selection with the device query replaced. The GPU tests build for the device's grid and the probed split
  counts, set a `VllmConfig` with custom ops on (the references construct `SiluAndMul` / `RMSNormGated`), and import
  the Gemma norm by name. The MI355 Buildkite job now also runs them with `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_GRID=128`,
  which covers the 128-CTA builds in CI (not run here: no MI355X available for this PR).

**K1 strict bit-exactness.** `DenseGdnTest` (strict equality with the stock GDN path) failed on this stack at every
width by about one bf16 ulp in ≈ 4 % of the core outputs; none of it was the 128-CTA decomposition. Three causes,
all fixed (`K1Build` fields from `stock_fields(rows, tp, oproj, cus)`):
- beta: K1 rounded `sigmoid(b)` to bf16, as `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` did before #53877
  ("Keep packed GDN decode beta in FP32"). K1 keeps it in fp32. This is the only change to the 256-CTA code objects.
- Gated norm layout: FLA's `layernorm_guard` gives a program two rows once rows x heads exceed 2 x CUs, which on 128
  CUs happens at 6+ rows (TP1) and 11+ (TP2), never at TP1 on 256 CUs. Its sum is then a thread's 4 columns as two
  pairs added elementwise, then xor 16 … 1 over 32 threads; K1 reproduces that order (`K1Build.norm_rows`,
  `tiling.gated_norm_rows`).
- TP2 out_proj split-K: probed from AITER like K2's (`K1Build.o_split`). Current AITER splits it in 3, which K1's
  out_proj partial cannot reproduce, so with K1's out_proj (the TP2 default) `dense_mono.py` refuses at startup and
  names the split (the self-check would fail anyway); `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_OPROJ=0` leaves out_proj stock.
  The strict test skips those widths.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- On MI350P the gain is limited to 1-4 decode rows (+12 to +19 % without MTP); at 8 rows mono is about equal to the
  stock path. The stock MXFP4 ASM GEMMs already reach 2.75-2.9 TB/s at one row on MI350P (≈ 3.1 TB/s achievable), so
  mono removes launch / glue overhead and the poorly utilized o_proj GEMM, not GEMM time; #61573's larger MI355X gain
  comes from the same overhead being a larger share of a step on a GPU with twice the bandwidth.
- MTP: mono helps at one and two requests (+19 %, +10 %); verify steps of three or more MTP-3 requests (12+ rows)
  are above the K1 / K2 builds (8 rows at TP1) and run stock. Adaptive (variable-length) verification runs stock.
- `spec_fused` reproduces the fused MTP kernel's 32-row tiles (its launch while requests x value heads < CUs, which
  holds for every verify step inside the 8-row caps); a wider tile is refused with a message.
- TP2 on 128 CUs is built and covered by the numerics tests but was not served; with current AITER it needs
  `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_OPROJ=0` (above).
- 10.8 GiB of shuffled weight copies (as in #61573); on MI350P the KV cache shrinks accordingly (2.79 M → 2.44 M
  tokens with MTP-3 on the nightly above).
- The best row caps depend on the stock MXFP4 decode GEMM (above); the defaults are the safe choice for both
  measured stacks.
- `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_GRID` is read like #61573's other `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_*` switches (not
  registered in `vllm/envs.py`).
- #61573's commits carry no `Signed-off-by` (DCO); this PR's do.
- Size: about 2,010 lines added and 500 removed under `vllm/` on top of #61573 (README included), of which
  `tiling.py` (460 lines) is the pass plans with their invariants and the geometry moved out of the kernel files.
- #61573 currently conflicts with main (`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`, `vllm/envs.py`,
  `vllm/models/qwen3_5/__init__.py`); this branch conflicts in the same three files only and is rebased once #61573
  is. On main, `vllm/models/qwen3_5/__init__.py` is now a hardware-split entry point (#61573's license-only file
  goes; `amd/` sits beside it) and `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` is no longer in `envs.py` (the hunk is re-anchored by
  hand). Applied that way on a recent nightly, the branch's kernels compile (K1 / K2 at TP1, including the
  verify-step builds) with no spills.

**Not a duplicate.** Open PRs searched for "mono decode 128", "MI350P mono", "dense mono": the closest is #63341
(DSv4.1 mono, draft), which resolves the grid from the CU count and refuses 128 pending the task decomposition
described in #63340; this PR does that decomposition for the Qwen3.8 dense kernels, with the width as a per-build
key field rather than a process-wide value.

detail.body:
## Overview

Dense mono decode for Qwen3.8-27B on 128-CU gfx950 (MI350P). **Stacked on #61573**, which adds the dense mono decode
for MI355X; the first two commits are #61573's and the rest are this PR's. Review the later commits. Draft until
#61573 lands.

AI assistance was used in developing this PR (code, tests, measurements and this description).

## Claims

- The K1 (GDN mixer) and K2 (MXFP4 FFN) persistent kernels of #61573 build and run with the grid width taken from the
  device's CU count: 256 (MI355X, MI350X) or 128 (MI350P). Other counts are refused with a message; #61573 refuses
  everything below 256 CUs.
- 256-CU builds are unchanged apart from one numerics fix: of the 80 K1 / K2 configurations, the 32 K2 compile to
  byte-identical code objects (sha256) with and without this PR, and the 48 K1 differ only by keeping beta in fp32
  (last bullet); with that line reverted all 80 are identical to #61573's.
- On MI350P (TP1, MTP off, same image, flag on vs off, default row caps): output throughput +19.1 % at one request
  (8k / 1k, TPOT 9.21 → 7.67 ms), +14.8 % at two, +12.0 % at four, +0.5 % at eight. Above the caps nothing changes.
- With MTP-3 (TP1), mono now runs the verify steps (until now the flag refused speculative decoding): K1 takes each
  request's 1 + 3 tokens through the conv and the recurrence in order, as vLLM's spec-decode kernels do, and K2 the
  rows. Output throughput +19.9 / +18.7 % at one request (two prompt seeds, TPOT 3.98 → 3.29 ms), +3.7 % at two
  (a verify step of two requests is 8 rows, above the default caps of 4), unchanged at four and eight. On a recent
  nightly whose stock MXFP4 decode GEMM is AITER's FlyDSL A4W4 kernel, one request gains about 6 % (verify step
  9.67 → 7.88 ms).
- Accuracy on MI350P is unchanged within run-to-run noise: GSM8K in the model card's setting (paired over three
  seeds, −0.18 ± 0.36 pt thinking, −0.45 ± 0.45 pt non-thinking), GSM8K chat, GPQA Diamond, RULER NIAH 64k / 128k;
  with MTP-3 at one request (K1 and K2 on every verify step), GSM8K card setting +0.53 ± 0.67 pt thinking,
  −0.68 ± 0.80 pt non-thinking.
- K1 and K2 are bit-exact on MI350P with the stock paths #61573's tests and startup checks compare against: K2 with
  the Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4` (TP1 S 1-8, TP2 S 1-16), K1 with the stock GDN decode (TP1 S 1-8; TP2 S 1-16 without
  out_proj; with out_proj see Details) and, on MTP-3 verify steps of one and two requests, with the spec-decode
  path vLLM serves: `causal_conv1d_update` with either the sigmoid-gated delta rule kernel + RMSNormGated (this
  base) or main's fused MTP decode kernel (#61855; checked on a recent nightly). A server that runs the MXFP4 linears on the AITER ASM GEMM (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`, as
  here) accumulates differently, so mono's greedy outputs are not byte-identical to that server's; accuracy is
  compared statistically.
- Fixes that apply to #61573 independently of the CU count: K2 follows the installed AITER's split-K (the bit-exact
  startup check failed with current AITER); the mono graph no longer takes over Model Runner V2's piecewise-cudagraph
  capture (the engine died on the first prefill); the GDN state-slot mapping runs once a step instead of in every GDN
  layer (144 launches a step); a GDN layer above K1's row cap no longer hands out_proj's output to K2 in place of its
  input (the skip hook was never installed); K1 rounded beta to bf16, which the stock decode kernel stopped doing
  in #53877 (K1's strict test failed by one bf16 ulp in ≈ 4 % of the outputs).

## Validation

Hardware: 1x MI350P (gfx950, 128 CUs, 4 XCDs), TP1, `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`. Image: vLLM v0.32.0 + AITER
main (2026-10-30) with the MI350P enablement PRs, FlyDSL 0.4.1, Triton 3.8.0 (`669b31ac`), and this branch's `vllm/`
Python files overlaid at a commit of this branch (`739f2c1d3e` for the tables without MTP, `1a10d1925f` for MTP;
the later commits make K1's spec l2 norm bit-exact). Mono arm: that image with `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1`; control arm: the same image with the flag
unset, except where a table says otherwise.

### Performance (`sglang.bench_serving`, random, range ratio 0.8)

Decode-bound cases, MTP off, both arms in the same image (control: flag unset):

| In / out | Conc | Out tok/s off → on (default caps 4) | Δ | TPOT p50 ms off → on | Out tok/s, caps 8 |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|
| 8192 / 1024 | 1 (seed 21) | 104.6 → 124.6 | +19.1 % | 9.21 → 7.67 | 124.3 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 1 (seed 22) | 105.0 → 125.0 | +19.1 % | 9.20 → 7.67 | 124.9 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 2 | 196.4 → 225.5 | +14.8 % | 9.83 → 8.52 | 224.7 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 344.3 → 385.6 | +12.0 % | 11.05 → 9.84 | 384.1 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 8 | 571.8 → 574.6 | +0.5 % | 13.19 → 13.19 | 579.1 (+1.3 %) |

With MTP-3 (`--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'`), branch at `1a10d1925f`, flag unset vs
set; K1 and K2 run the verify steps (a request's verify step is 4 rows):

| In / out | Conc | Out tok/s MTP-3 → + mono (default caps 4) | Δ | TPOT p50 ms | Out tok/s, caps 8 | Δ |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| 8192 / 1024 | 1 (seed 21) | 223.7 → 268.2 | +19.9 % | 3.98 → 3.29 | 267.0 | +19.4 % |
| 8192 / 1024 | 1 (seed 22) | 222.7 → 264.3 | +18.7 % | 3.76 → 3.19 | 266.7 | +19.7 % |
| 8192 / 1024 | 2 | 353.3 → 366.4 | +3.7 % | 5.22 → 5.10 | 389.4 | +10.2 % |
| 8192 / 1024 | 4 | 592.7 → 592.1 | −0.1 % | 5.97 → 5.98 | 591.1 | −0.3 % |
| 8192 / 1024 | 8 | 930.4 → 932.9 | +0.3 % | 7.67 → 7.65 | 934.1 | +0.4 % |

Prompts: 8 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 at concurrency 1 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 8, warmup = concurrency. One run per cell. Without MTP
the two concurrency-1 seeds agree within 0.4 %, and controls on different images (identical outside mono) within
1.5 % (`739f2c1d3e` vs `1a10d1925f`, flag unset, MTP off: 104.6 / 105.0 vs 103.0 / 104.7 at one request). With caps 4
a verify step of two requests (8 rows) runs stock; caps 8 run it through K1 + K2, +10.2 % here, where the stock MXFP4
linears are the AITER ASM GEMM. On a recent nightly (vLLM main, same MI350P, MTP-3) whose stock decode GEMM is AITER's
FlyDSL A4W4 kernel, the same 8-row steps ran about 5 % slower than stock (412.6 / 407.4 vs 432.8 / 433.4 tok/s at
two requests; caps 4: 431.8), so the default caps stay 4 with speculative decoding; one request there: verify step
9.67 → 7.88 ms, 4k / 1k output throughput +6.5 %, four and more requests within −1 … +3 %. With K2 alone on the verify steps (an earlier commit, K1 off)
the gain at one request was +4.9 % and none at two. TTFT is unchanged (prefill takes the stock path).

Wider and prefill-bound cases (control: the base image; mono does not run above 8 rows):

| In / out | Conc | Out tok/s off → on | Δ | TPOT p50 ms off → on |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| 8192 / 1024 | 16 | 878.8 → 883.6 | +0.5 % | 17.21 → 17.10 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 32 | 1181.9 → 1188.0 | +0.5 % | 25.25 → 25.13 |
| 8192 / 1024 | 64 | 1471.7 → 1477.2 | +0.4 % | 40.66 → 40.44 |
| 128000 / 1024 | 4 | 82.7 → 84.0 | +1.6 % | 37.95 → 37.19 |
| 128000 / 1024 | 8 | 92.6 → 92.5 | −0.1 % | 73.13 → 73.25 |

96 / 128 / 256 prompts at concurrency 16 / 32 / 64, 32 / 64 at 128k; an earlier build of this branch (`d6ede56f1a`,
row caps 8) vs the base image without this branch.

Per launch on MI350P (CUDA-graph replay, real shapes): K2 67 / 70 / 79 µs and K1 27.6 / 40.5 / 58 µs at 1 / 4 / 8
rows.
At 8 rows a torch-profiler trace shows K1 + K2 taking about as long as the stock kernels they replace (the MI350P
MXFP4 ASM GEMMs run gate_up at M = 8 in 34 µs, about the bandwidth K2's GEMM phases reach); at 1-4 rows mono saves
the per-kernel launch and activation-quantization overhead of the stock path. #61573 reports larger gains on
MI355X (+34 % at concurrency 4), where the stock path is further from its bandwidth bound.

### Accuracy

MTP off, row caps 8, branch at `0846b5d5a2`. The later commits change K1's decode outputs only by moving
them onto the stock path's bits (fp32 beta, the gated norm's reduction order; at most one bf16 ulp in ≈ 4 % of the
outputs before) and leave K2's unchanged (the state-slot mapping is the same indices; the per-CTA norm gives a
bit-identical x, checked: in_proj_qkvz bit-exact with the stock GEMM), so these results stand for the head. At 8 concurrent requests the decode steps stay inside the
caps, so K1 and K2 produce nearly every generated token; at 16 and 32 they mostly do not, so those rows check the
flag-on server rather than the kernels.

| Eval | Concurrency | non-mono | mono |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K 5-shot, chat template, thinking off, greedy, 250 questions, flexible / strict | 8 | 0.920 / 0.916 | 0.932 / 0.916 |
| GPQA Diamond, thinking on, greedy, max 32k tokens, 198 questions | 8 | 0.773 | 0.768 |
| RULER `niah_single_2` 64k, 50 samples | 8 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| RULER `niah_single_2` 128k, 50 samples | 8 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| GSM8K 5-shot, chat template, thinking off, greedy, 250 questions, flexible / strict | 32 | 0.920 / 0.912 | 0.920 / 0.916 |
| GPQA Diamond, thinking on, greedy, max 32k tokens, 198 questions | 16 | 0.778 | 0.778 |

GPQA's standard error at 198 questions is about 0.03 (the 0.005 difference is one question); GSM8K's at 250 about
0.017. One run per cell.

GSM8K in the model card's setting (`lm_eval` `local-completions`, 5-shot, full 1319 questions, sampled; thinking:
task `gsm8k`, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, max_gen_toks 3072; non-thinking: the card's `gsm8k_nothink`
task, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, presence_penalty 1.5; card: 94.996 / 89.92 flexible), 8 concurrent, both arms on
the same image, three repeats per arm with request seeds 2004-2006 (the same seed in both arms of a repeat):

| Mode | non-mono, flexible-extract | mono, flexible-extract | mono − non-mono, paired |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Thinking | 0.9356 / 0.9272 / 0.9371 (mean 0.9333) | 0.9318 / 0.9295 / 0.9333 (mean 0.9315) | −0.18 ± 0.36 pt |
| Non-thinking | 0.8969 / 0.8961 / 0.9030 (mean 0.8987) | 0.8954 / 0.8908 / 0.8961 (mean 0.8941) | −0.45 ± 0.45 pt |

(± is one standard error of the per-question paired difference over the 3 × 1319 question runs.) Three earlier
repeats per arm all sent lm-eval's default request seed (1234), so they differ only through batch-dependent numerics
and are not independent draws; they give thinking 0.940 / 0.948 / 0.948 vs 0.939 / 0.935 / 0.931 and non-thinking
0.901 / 0.893 / 0.904 vs 0.912 / 0.895 / 0.907. Over all six runs per arm: thinking 0.939 vs 0.933, non-thinking
0.899 vs 0.899.

With MTP-3, one request at a time (a verify step of one request is 4 rows, inside the cap), the same request seed
(2004) in both arms; branch at `f70f45a7c4` (K1 and K2 on the verify steps), and for comparison `739f2c1d3e` (K2
only, K1 off):

| Mode | MTP-3, flexible / strict | MTP-3 + mono, flexible / strict | mono − MTP-3, paired (flexible) | Eval wall time |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Thinking, K1 + K2 | 0.9265 / 0.9227 | 0.9318 / 0.9333 | +0.53 ± 0.67 pt | 23:45 → 18:38 |
| Non-thinking, K1 + K2 | 0.8961 / 0.8969 | 0.8893 / 0.8878 | −0.68 ± 0.80 pt | 14:12 → 11:55 |
| Thinking, K2 only | 0.9265 / 0.9227 | 0.9303 / 0.9356 | +0.38 ± 0.69 pt | 23:15 → 22:27 |
| Non-thinking, K2 only | 0.8961 / 0.8969 | 0.8908 / 0.8908 | −0.53 ± 0.76 pt | 14:09 → 13:33 |

(The MTP-3 arm is the same server in both pairs; its two runs gave identical scores.)

`lm_eval` (`local-chat-completions` for GSM8K chat and NIAH, `local-completions` for the card-setting GSM8K) and
`sglang.test.run_eval` (GPQA) against the servers.

### Kernel numerics (MI350P, grid 128)

```
pytest tests/models/qwen3_5/test_amd_dense_mono_tiling.py   # CPU only
55 passed
pytest -v tests/models/qwen3_5/test_amd_dense_mono.py
DenseFfnTest::test_bit_exact        PASSED  (K2 TP1, S 1-8 x 512 draws, bit-exact)
DenseFfnTest::test_bit_exact_tp2    PASSED  (K2 TP2 partials, 2 ranks x S 1-16 x 512)
DenseGdnTest::test_bit_exact*       PASSED  (K1 TP1 S 1-8, TP2 S 1-16 without out_proj, bit-exact)
DenseGdnSpecTest::test_verify_steps PASSED  (K1 on MTP-3 verify steps, 1 and 2 requests, bit-exact)
DenseGdnSpecTest::test_verify_steps_fused SKIPPED  (this base has no fused MTP decode kernel)
StockChainTest, StockSplitTest, StockAccumulationTest, RowCapsTest   PASSED
10 passed, 17 skipped (16: TP2 K1 with out_proj, AITER splits it in 3), 231 subtests passed
```

The same file with this branch's `amd/` package on a recent nightly (vLLM main with #61855, same MI350P): 11 passed,
16 skipped, 295 subtests passed; `test_verify_steps_fused` bit-exact against `fused_gdn_decode_post_conv_mtp`. A
server on that nightly with MTP-3 and the flag passes the startup self-check and runs mono verify steps.

### Compile-only, no GPU (FlyDSL 0.4.1, `COMPILE_ONLY=1 ARCH=gfx950`)

80 configurations (TP1 K2 S 1-8 with and without `oproj`; TP1 K1 S 1-8, first layer and not; TP2 K2 S 1-16; TP2
K1 S 1-16 with and without `out_proj`), each for #61573, this PR at 256 CTAs and this PR at 128 CTAs: all compile;
the 256-CTA code objects are identical to #61573's except K1's fp32 beta (identical with it reverted); no VGPR spills
or scratch at either width (max 247 VGPRs at 128 CTAs, K1 TP1 at 8 rows; TP2 K1 has SGPR spills to VGPR lanes, as
in #61573). The K1 verify-step builds (`spec=4`, S 4 and 8, first layer and not) compile at both widths with no
spills (max 218 VGPRs), and the spec changes leave all 160 non-spec code objects unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce</summary>

```bash
# server (flag on; drop the three mono variables for the control arm)
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1 \
VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE=1 VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_K1_MAX_ROWS=8 VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_K2_MAX_ROWS=8 \
vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN --gdn-prefill-backend aiter_flydsl --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --no-enable-prefix-caching
# with MTP-3 (mono is then K2 only): add --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
# benchmark (one case)
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend vllm --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 0.8 --request-rate inf --max-concurrency 4 \
  --num-prompts 32 --warmup-requests 4 --seed 1 --model amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4
# GSM8K, model card setting (thinking; non-thinking: --tasks gsm8k_nothink with the card's task file and gen_kwargs)
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --seed 1234   --model_args model=amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,tokenizer=amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4,num_concurrent=8,max_retries=5,timeout=900,tokenized_requests=False,max_length=16384,seed=2004   --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=3072,temperature=1.0,top_p=0.95,top_k=20,min_p=0.0,presence_penalty=0.0,repetition_penalty=1.0,do_sample=True
# kernel numerics; on a 256-CU GPU, VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_GRID=128 runs the 128-CTA builds
pytest -v tests/models/qwen3_5/test_amd_dense_mono_tiling.py tests/models/qwen3_5/test_amd_dense_mono.py
```

</details>

## Details

**Why #61573 does not run on 128 CUs.** K1 and K2 run one CTA per CU, all co-resident, exchanging data through
spin-waited mailboxes, so the grid must equal the CU count; #61573 hard-codes 256 and refuses smaller GPUs (a
256-CTA grid would deadlock on 128 CUs). Several stage layouts also assume 256: one o_proj owner per CTA for 160
owners, one whole down row group per CTA (320 = 256 + 64 split), 4 in_proj_qkvz groups per CTA filling the 8 waves,
and the flag / scratch regions sized by 256.

**What changed.**
- `mono/tiling.py` (new, pure Python): `resolve_grid(cus, override)` picks the width (256, 128; else `ValueError`
  naming the validated widths); `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_GRID` may select a validated width at most the CU
  count (to run the 128-CTA build on a 256-CU GPU). The FFN / GDN geometries move here with the grid as a field,
  plus the per-stage pass plans and their invariants (checked at import for both widths).
- K1 / K2 (`dense_gdn.py`, `dense_ffn.py`): the grid is a field of the build key (so it is in FlyDSL's JIT key; the
  128-CTA kernel symbols end in `_g128`). Stages whose tasks outnumber the CTAs take more passes per CTA, each task
  computed exactly as before: o_proj / out_proj / K1 front owners `bid + p * grid` (a second pass on CTAs 0..31 at
  128); in_proj_qkvz in passes of 4 groups; down's whole row groups and its split group in tile passes; gate_up 8
  whole groups and 8 columns of a split one per CTA; GDN tasks in one pass at TP1 (up to 48 tasks) and in passes of
  whole tokens at TP2 above 24 (a token's tasks all run in the same pass, so no CTA waits on a later pass). At 256
  every stage is one pass and the traced program is unchanged (offsets of 0 emit nothing; the down store keeps its
  original form).
- `dense_mono.py`: refuses with the resolver's message instead of `< 256`; passes the grid to both build keys; a
  build wider than the device's CUs raises instead of hanging.
- K2 split-K: K2 is bit-exact with the stock Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4` only if it splits K the same way. #61573
  hard-codes 4 / 4 / 2 splits; AITER's current `get_splitk` gives gate_up 2, down 2 at TP1 and 1 at TP2 (not
  CU-dependent), so #61573's startup self-check refuses to start with current AITER. K2 probes the stock split
  counts once per width at startup and builds them (`FfnBuild.gu_split / d_split / o_split`; 0 keeps the default).
  Without the probe `DenseFfnTest::test_bit_exact` fails on this stack; `StockSplitTest` checks the probe against
  AITER's `get_splitk`. The probe runs once in model preparation, so there is no new host synchronization in
  steady-state decode.
- Model Runner V2: its PIECEWISE cudagraphs for the stock model are captured by dummy steps that look like pure
  decode; #61573's mono graph took them over, the stock piecewise graphs for widths up to the cap were never
  captured, and the first prefill of such a width tried to capture at run time on the default stream
  (`CUDA graphs must be captured on a non-default stream`). The mono graph now skips PIECEWISE runtime-mode steps;
  pure decode runs under FULL cudagraphs and still takes it. Reproducer: the serve command below with the flag on
  and any request; before the fix the engine dies on its first prefill, after it the smoke requests, the benchmarks
  and the evals above run. Not covered by a unit test (it needs a capturing engine).
- K1 front on 128 CTAs (up to 4 rows): every CTA runs the input norm on the whole rows itself with K2's
  `run_norm`, which reduces in the owners' order, in place of 160 owner tasks (a second pass on CTAs 0..31) and two
  grid-wide hand-offs. x is bit-identical; K1 27.6 / 32.3 / 40.5 µs at 1 / 2 / 4 rows (was 30.3 / 35.1 / 43.5).
  Wider steps keep the owners (the kept rows spill there). 256-CTA builds keep the owners.
- GDN state slots: the copy + null-slot mapping of the state indices ran in every GDN layer (3 launches x 48); GDN
  layers of a KV-cache group share the indices, so it runs once per group a step. −0.5 ms of GPU time a step at one
  request.
- Speculative decoding (TP1): `K1Build.spec` = tokens a request in a verify step (1 + k). A GDN task becomes a
  request's tokens in order: the conv slides its window from offset `n_acc - 1` and rewrites the widened conv state
  (slot `idx[r, 0]`, length 2 + spec), the recurrence starts from slot `idx[r, n_acc - 1]` and stores each token's
  state to `idx[r, j]`, null slots (≤ 0) are skipped — the semantics of
  `causal_conv1d_update(num_accepted_tokens=…)` and `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update(ssm_state_indices=[R,
  1 + k])`. The spec kernel holds one q / k element a lane over two waves, so on spec builds K1's l2 norm reduces each
  wave and adds the two sums (bit-exact; with the decode kernel's order the core differed by one bf16 ulp in a few
  elements a step). The accepted counts ride in the `w_os` argument (unused without out_proj), so the kernel ABI and
  the non-spec code objects are unchanged. `dense_mono.py` reads vLLM's persistent spec buffers and enters only whole
  verify steps (requests x (1 + k) == rows, from tensor shapes, no host sync); partial verify steps and warm-up
  batches run stock. A startup self-check runs K1 on verify steps against the stock spec kernels and an fp32
  reference. Where the GDN layers serve verify steps with the fused MTP decode kernel
  (`enable_fused_gdn_spec_decode`; main since #61855), `K1Build.spec_fused` takes its numerics: launched, it keeps the
  decode kernel's state layout, so the recurrence is unchanged, but its q / k l2 norm sums each of two warps with
  the first DPP step contracted into an fma, and its gated norm sums the squares in tiles of 32 rows (rows 16 apart
  contracted, then xor 8 … 1; tiles added (t0 + t2) + (t1 + t3)); the self-check then compares against that kernel.
  The default caps (4) take a verify step of one MTP-3 request. With K1 switched off, each GDN layer is the compiled stock layer up to out_proj's input (a shallow
  view with out_proj as passthrough, so inductor fuses it as in the stock graph) and K2 takes the rows. TP2 still
  refuses speculative decoding.
- Tests: `test_amd_dense_mono_tiling.py` (new, CPU only, wired into the existing Buildkite job) replays every
  stage's task placement at both widths (each task exactly once; GDN passes closed under their hand-offs) and checks
  the grid selection with the device query replaced. The GPU tests build for the device's grid and the probed split
  counts, set a `VllmConfig` with custom ops on (the references construct `SiluAndMul` / `RMSNormGated`), and import
  the Gemma norm by name. The MI355 Buildkite job now also runs them with `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_GRID=128`,
  which covers the 128-CTA builds in CI (not run here: no MI355X available for this PR).

**K1 strict bit-exactness.** `DenseGdnTest` (strict equality with the stock GDN path) failed on this stack at every
width by about one bf16 ulp in ≈ 4 % of the core outputs; none of it was the 128-CTA decomposition. Three causes,
all fixed (`K1Build` fields from `stock_fields(rows, tp, oproj, cus)`):
- beta: K1 rounded `sigmoid(b)` to bf16, as `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` did before #53877
  ("Keep packed GDN decode beta in FP32"). K1 keeps it in fp32. This is the only change to the 256-CTA code objects.
- Gated norm layout: FLA's `layernorm_guard` gives a program two rows once rows x heads exceed 2 x CUs, which on 128
  CUs happens at 6+ rows (TP1) and 11+ (TP2), never at TP1 on 256 CUs. Its sum is then a thread's 4 columns as two
  pairs added elementwise, then xor 16 … 1 over 32 threads; K1 reproduces that order (`K1Build.norm_rows`,
  `tiling.gated_norm_rows`).
- TP2 out_proj split-K: probed from AITER like K2's (`K1Build.o_split`). Current AITER splits it in 3, which K1's
  out_proj partial cannot reproduce, so with K1's out_proj (the TP2 default) `dense_mono.py` refuses at startup and
  names the split (the self-check would fail anyway); `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_OPROJ=0` leaves out_proj stock.
  The strict test skips those widths.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- On MI350P the gain is limited to 1-4 decode rows (+12 to +19 % without MTP); at 8 rows mono is about equal to the
  stock path. The stock MXFP4 ASM GEMMs already reach 2.75-2.9 TB/s at one row on MI350P (≈ 3.1 TB/s achievable), so
  mono removes launch / glue overhead and the poorly utilized o_proj GEMM, not GEMM time; #61573's larger MI355X gain
  comes from the same overhead being a larger share of a step on a GPU with twice the bandwidth.
- MTP: mono helps at one and two requests (+19 %, +10 %); verify steps of three or more MTP-3 requests (12+ rows)
  are above the K1 / K2 builds (8 rows at TP1) and run stock. Adaptive (variable-length) verification runs stock.
- `spec_fused` reproduces the fused MTP kernel's 32-row tiles (its launch while requests x value heads < CUs, which
  holds for every verify step inside the 8-row caps); a wider tile is refused with a message.
- TP2 on 128 CUs is built and covered by the numerics tests but was not served; with current AITER it needs
  `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_OPROJ=0` (above).
- 10.8 GiB of shuffled weight copies (as in #61573); on MI350P the KV cache shrinks accordingly (2.79 M → 2.44 M
  tokens with MTP-3 on the nightly above).
- The best row caps depend on the stock MXFP4 decode GEMM (above); the defaults are the safe choice for both
  measured stacks.
- `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_GRID` is read like #61573's other `VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_*` switches (not
  registered in `vllm/envs.py`).
- #61573's commits carry no `Signed-off-by` (DCO); this PR's do.
- Size: about 2,010 lines added and 500 removed under `vllm/` on top of #61573 (README included), of which
  `tiling.py` (460 lines) is the pass plans with their invariants and the geometry moved out of the kernel files.
- #61573 currently conflicts with main (`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml`, `vllm/envs.py`,
  `vllm/models/qwen3_5/__init__.py`); this branch conflicts in the same three files only and is rebased once #61573
  is. On main, `vllm/models/qwen3_5/__init__.py` is now a hardware-split entry point (#61573's license-only file
  goes; `amd/` sits beside it) and `VLLM_ROCM_MONO_DECODE` is no longer in `envs.py` (the hunk is re-anchored by
  hand). Applied that way on a recent nightly, the branch's kernels compile (K1 / K2 at TP1, including the
  verify-step builds) with no spills.

**Not a duplicate.** Open PRs searched for "mono decode 128", "MI350P mono", "dense mono": the closest is #63341
(DSv4.1 mono, draft), which resolves the grid from the CU count and refuses 128 pending the task decomposition
described in #63340; this PR does that decomposition for the Qwen3.8 dense kernels, with the width as a per-build
key field rather than a process-wide value.

@@ -0,0 +1,917 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Bit-exactness of the Qwen3.8-27B dense mono decode kernels (ROCm / FlyDSL,
+gfx950) against the stock decode path, on random MXFP4 weights.
+
+``DenseFfnTest`` (K2, ``dense_ffn``): out_proj / o_proj + the residual add +
+post_attention_layernorm + gate_up, SiLU-mul and down, against dynamic_mxfp4_quant
++ Triton ``gemm_afp4wfp4``, the ROCm Triton Gemma norm and SiluAndMul. At TP2
+(from the stock norm's output) each rank's down partial before the all-reduce,
+from its half of gate_up's rows and down's K columns.
+
+``RowCapsTest``: K1's and K2's row caps by TP and their env overrides.
+
+``StockAccumulationTest``: on typical inputs at K2's K sizes the stock MXFP4
+GEMM's output is bf16(fp32(exact sum)), so a mismatch there is a K2 bug rather
+than a rounding corner. ``StockSplitTest``: the split counts K2 follows are the
+stock GEMM's at every width. ``StockChainTest``: K2 is exact by construction, on
+rows whose exact sums need more than 24 bits, where the same GEMMs summed in K
+quarters differ from stock.
+
+``DenseGdnTest`` (K1, ``dense_gdn``): the residual add + input_layernorm ->
+in_proj_qkvz / in_proj_ba -> conv1d -> the gated delta rule -> the gated norm,
+against the ROCm Triton Gemma norm, the MXFP4 linears, ``causal_conv1d_update``,
+``fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode`` and RMSNormGated. The core,
+the residual and both states must match, on the first layer (no residual) and
+with pad rows (slot -1); other slots stay untouched. At TP2 (from the stock input
+norm's output, as the runtime runs it there) each rank's half of the heads, its
+column-parallel slices of the same layer, against the stock path on them, with
+out_proj folded in (its partial, from the rank's K columns) and without.
+
+Widths 1..8 at TP1 and 1..16 at TP2, each with its own weights and Mailbox
+layer tag, over many input draws: a norm reduced in another order than the stock
+kernel's still matches on most rows, and shows on about one row in 640.
+Run directly with ``pytest tests/models/qwen3_5/test_amd_dense_mono.py``.
+
+The kernels build for the GPU's grid (``tiling.device_grid``: 256 CTAs on
+MI355X, 128 on MI350P). ``VLLM_ROCM_QWEN38_DENSE_MONO_GRID=128`` runs the
+128-CTA builds on a 256-CU GPU.
+"""
+
+import os
+import unittest
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+
+import torch
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _env(name, value):
+    old = os.environ.get(name)
+    if value is None:
+        os.environ.pop(name, None)
+    else:
+        os.environ[name] = value
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        if old is None:
+            os.environ.pop(name, None)
+        else:
+            os.environ[name] = old
+
+
+BF = torch.bfloat16
+EPS = 1e-6
+FFN_DRAWS = 512
+GDN_DRAWS = 512
+# Mailbox tag slots: the layer index a launch passes as ``layer``.
+LAYER_TAGS = (0, 17, 63)
+
+
+def _gfx950() -> bool:
+    return (
+        torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.version.hip is not None
+        and "gfx950" in torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).gcnArchName
+    )
+
+
+def _mxfp4(g, n, k):
+    """Random MXFP4 [n, k]: fp4 pairs and e8m0 scales 2^-7 .. 2^-1."""
+    w = torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (n, k // 2), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda", generator=g
+    )
+    ws = torch.randint(
+        120, 127, (n, k // 32), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda", generator=g
+    )
+    return w, ws
+
+
+_CONFIG = None
+
+
+def setUpModule():
+    """A VllmConfig for the stock custom ops the references build (SiluAndMul,
+    RMSNormGated), as tests/conftest.py's ``default_vllm_config``, with every
+    custom op on: the kernels match the ops' ROCm kernels (the eager serving
+    path), not their PyTorch-native fallbacks."""
+    global _CONFIG
+    from vllm.config import CompilationConfig, VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+
+    _CONFIG = set_current_vllm_config(
+        VllmConfig(compilation_config=CompilationConfig(custom_ops=["all"]))
+    )
+    _CONFIG.__enter__()
+
+
+def tearDownModule():
+    if _CONFIG is not None:
+        _CONFIG.__exit__(None, None, None)
+
+
+def _cus():
+    """The GPU's compute units (the stock gated norm's layout follows them)."""
+    from vllm.models.qwen3_5.amd.mono.tiling import _resident_cus
+
+    return _resident_cus()
+
+
+def _grid():
+    """The grid the kernels build for on this GPU."""
+    from vllm.models.qwen3_5.amd.mono.tiling import device_grid
+
+    return device_grid()
+
+
+def _widths(tp):
+    from vllm.models.qwen3_5.amd.mono import dense_ffn as D
+
+    return range(1, D.max_tokens(tp) + 1)
+
+
+def _rnd(g, *shape, scale=1.0, dtype=BF):
+    return (torch.randn(*shape, generator=g, device="cuda") * scale).to(dtype)
+
+
+def _linear(x, w, ws):
+    from aiter.ops.triton.gemm_afp4wfp4 import gemm_afp4wfp4
+    from aiter.ops.triton.quant import dynamic_mxfp4_quant
+
+    xq, xs = dynamic_mxfp4_quant(x)
+    y = torch.empty(x.size(0), w.size(0), dtype=BF, device=x.device)
+    gemm_afp4wfp4(xq, w, xs, ws, BF, y)
+    return y
+
+
+def _k_cols(w, ws, k, tp, rank):
+    """Row-parallel: the rank's input columns of an MXFP4 [n, k]."""
+    n = k // tp
+    return (
+        w[:, rank * n // 2 : (rank + 1) * n // 2].contiguous(),
+        ws[:, rank * n // 32 : (rank + 1) * n // 32].contiguous(),
+    )
+
+
+_FP4 = (0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 6, -0.0, -0.5, -1, -1.5, -2, -3, -4, -6)
+
+
+def _dequant(wq, ws):
+    """MXFP4 [n, k / 2] (low nibble the even column), e8m0 [n, k / 32] -> fp64."""
+    lut = torch.tensor(_FP4, dtype=torch.float64, device=wq.device)
+    v = torch.stack([lut[(wq & 0xF).long()], lut[(wq >> 4).long()]], -1)
+    s = torch.pow(2.0, ws.double() - 127.0).repeat_interleave(32, dim=1)
+    return v.reshape(wq.size(0), -1) * s
+
+
+def _gemma_norm(x, residual, w):
+    """GemmaRMSNorm as the stock path runs it on ROCm with aiter -> x, residual."""
+    # a from-import: the ops package re-exports a ``gemma_rmsnorm`` function that
+    # shadows the module of the same name as an attribute
+    from vllm.models.minimax_m3.amd.ops.gemma_rmsnorm import (
+        gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm,
+        gemma_rmsnorm,
+    )
+
+    if residual is None:
+        return gemma_rmsnorm(x, w, EPS), x
+    return gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm(x, residual, w, EPS)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(_gfx950(), "needs FlyDSL and aiter on gfx950")
+class DenseFfnTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_bit_exact(self):
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.activation import SiluAndMul
+        from vllm.models.qwen3_5.amd.mono import dense_ffn as D
+
+        act = SiluAndMul()
+        for s in _widths(1):
+            g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(s)
+            layer = LAYER_TAGS[s % len(LAYER_TAGS)]
+            w_o, w_os = _mxfp4(g, D.HIDDEN, D.CORE)
+            w13, w13s = _mxfp4(g, 2 * D.INTER, D.HIDDEN)
+            w2, w2s = _mxfp4(g, D.HIDDEN, D.INTER)
+            ln_w = _rnd(g, D.HIDDEN, scale=0.1)
+            weights = dict(
+                w_o=D.shuffle_w(w_o),
+                w_os=w_os,
+                ln_w=ln_w,
+                w13=D.shuffle_w(w13),
+                w13s=w13s,
+                w2=D.shuffle_w(w2),
+                w2s=w2s,
+            )
+            key = D.FfnBuild(
+                tokens=s,
+                eps=EPS,
+                shuffled=True,
+                oproj=True,
+                grid=_grid(),
+                **D.stock_split_fields(s, 1, True),
+            )
+            out = torch.empty(s, D.HIDDEN, dtype=BF, device="cuda")
+            res_out = torch.empty_like(out)
+            epoch = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+            # One scratch for every launch: the epoch tags must keep it valid.
+            scratch = torch.zeros(
+                D.scratch_bytes(key), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"
+            )
+            bad = []
+            for draw in range(FFN_DRAWS):
+                core = _rnd(g, s, D.CORE, scale=0.5)
+                residual = _rnd(g, s, D.HIDDEN, scale=2.0)
+                x, res_ref = _gemma_norm(_linear(core, w_o, w_os), residual, ln_w)
+                out_ref = _linear(act(_linear(x, w13, w13s)), w2, w2s)
+                epoch.add_(1)
+                D.dense_ffn(
+                    key,
+                    hidden=core,
+                    residual=residual,
+                    out=out,
+                    res_out=res_out,
+                    scratch=scratch,
+                    epoch=epoch,
+                    layer=layer,
+                    **weights,
+                )
+                if not (torch.equal(res_out, res_ref) and torch.equal(out, out_ref)):
+                    bad.append(draw)
+            with self.subTest(s=s, layer=layer):
+                self.assertEqual(bad, [])
+
+    def test_bit_exact_tp2(self):
+        from vllm.model_executor.layers.activation import SiluAndMul
+        from vllm.models.qwen3_5.amd.mono import dense_ffn as D
+
+        act = SiluAndMul()
+        inter = D.FGeo(2).inter
+        for rank in range(2):
+            for s in _widths(2):
+                g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(200 + s)
+                layer = LAYER_TAGS[s % len(LAYER_TAGS)]
+                w13, w13s = _mxfp4(g, 2 * D.INTER, D.HIDDEN)
+                w2, w2s = _mxfp4(g, D.HIDDEN, D.INTER)
+                ln_w = _rnd(g, D.HIDDEN, scale=0.1)
+                # Column-parallel gate_up: the rank's half of gate, then of up.
+                rows = [
+                    slice(o + rank * inter, o + (rank + 1) * inter)
+                    for o in (0, D.INTER)
+                ]
+                w13 = torch.cat([w13[r] for r in rows]).contiguous()
+                w13s = torch.cat([w13s[r] for r in rows]).contiguous()
+                w2, w2s = _k_cols(w2, w2s, D.INTER, 2, rank)
+                w13_sh, w2_sh = D.shuffle_w(w13), D.shuffle_w(w2)
+                key = D.FfnBuild(
+                    tokens=s,
+                    shuffled=True,
+                    tp=2,
+                    normed=True,
+                    grid=_grid(),
+                    **D.stock_split_fields(s, 2, False),
+                )
+                out = torch.empty(s, D.HIDDEN, dtype=BF, device="cuda")
+                epoch = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+                scratch = torch.zeros(
+                    D.scratch_bytes(key), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"
+                )
+                bad = []
+                for draw in range(FFN_DRAWS // 2):
+                    h = _rnd(g, s, D.HIDDEN, scale=0.5)
+                    x, _ = _gemma_norm(h, _rnd(g, s, D.HIDDEN, scale=2.0), ln_w)
+                    out_ref = _linear(act(_linear(x, w13, w13s)), w2, w2s)
+                    epoch.add_(1)
+                    D.dense_ffn(
+                        key,
+                        hidden=x,
+                        residual=None,
+                        ln_w=None,
+                        w13=w13_sh,
+                        w13s=w13s,
+                        w2=w2_sh,
+                        w2s=w2s,
+                        out=out,
+                        res_out=None,
+                        scratch=scratch,
+                        epoch=epoch,
+                        layer=layer,
+                    )
+                    if not torch.equal(out, out_ref):
+                        bad.append(draw)
+                with self.subTest(rank=rank, s=s, layer=layer):
+                    self.assertEqual(bad, [])
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(_gfx950(), "needs FlyDSL and aiter on gfx950")
+class RowCapsTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_tp_defaults_and_overrides(self):
+        from vllm.models.qwen3_5.amd.dense_mono import row_caps
+
+        cases = (
+            (None, None, (4, 4), (8, 8)),

+def _linear_parts(x, w, ws, splits=None, block_k=128):
+    """The stock GEMM's fp32 split partials [n, M, N] (``splits``: forced to
+    that many equal K splits), or its bf16 output [M, N] for one split."""
+    from aiter.ops.triton.gemm_afp4wfp4 import gemm_afp4wfp4
+    from aiter.ops.triton.quant import dynamic_mxfp4_quant
+
+    xq, xs = dynamic_mxfp4_quant(x)
+    cfg = None
+    if splits is not None:
+        cfg = dict(
+            BLOCK_SIZE_M=16,
+            BLOCK_SIZE_N=64,
+            BLOCK_SIZE_K=block_k,
+            GROUP_SIZE_M=1,
+            num_warps=4,
+            num_stages=2,
+            waves_per_eu=2,
+            matrix_instr_nonkdim=16,
+            cache_modifier=None,
+            NUM_KSPLIT=splits,
+        )

+def _linear_quartered(x, w, ws):
+    """The GEMM as four K quarters, each chained from zero, summed in order."""
+    p = _linear_parts(x, w, ws, splits=4)
+    assert p.dim() == 3 and p.size(0) == 4
+    return (((p[0] + p[1]) + p[2]) + p[3]).to(BF)

+def _cancel_blocks(w, ws, rows, blocks, g):
+    """Rows ``rows`` of an MXFP4 [n, k] zeroed but for ``blocks``: (block, kind),
+    kind "big" (random fp4, scale 2^30), "neg" (the previous big block negated)
+    or "small" (random, scale 2^0)."""
+    k_blocks = ws.size(1)
+    for r in rows:
+        w[r] = 0
+        ws[r] = 127
+        prev = None
+        for b, kind in blocks:
+            assert 0 <= b < k_blocks
+            cols = slice(16 * b, 16 * b + 16)
+            if kind == "neg":
+                w[r, cols] = w[r, 16 * prev : 16 * prev + 16] ^ 0x88
+                ws[r, b] = ws[r, prev]
+                continue
+            w[r, cols] = torch.randint(
+                0, 256, (16,), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda", generator=g
+            )
+            ws[r, b] = 157 if kind == "big" else 127
+            prev = b
+

+def _copy_block(t, dst, src):
+    """Columns 32 dst .. of ``t`` (bf16 [.., k]) := columns 32 src .."""
+    t[..., 32 * dst : 32 * dst + 32] = t[..., 32 * src : 32 * src + 32]

+class StockChainTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """K2 reproduces the stock GEMMs' arithmetic, not only their exact sums: on
+    rows whose exact sums span more than 24 bits (a 2^30-scaled block and its
+    negation, small blocks next to them), stock differs from the same GEMMs
+    summed in K quarters, and K2 still matches stock. Gate rows (seen through
+    down rows reading only their columns) and down rows each get a pair across
+    a quarter boundary inside a split (P1) and across the split boundary (P2)."""
+
+    def _weights(self, g, hidden, inter):
+        w13, w13s = _mxfp4(g, 2 * inter, hidden)
+        w2, w2s = _mxfp4(g, hidden, inter)
+        for w, ws, rows, k in ((w13, w13s, (0, 4), hidden), (w2, w2s, (0, 4), inter)):
+            nb = k // 32
+            qb, sb = nb // 4, nb // 2
+            p1 = [(qb - 1, "big"), (qb, "neg"), (qb + 1, "small")]
+            p2 = [(1, "small"), (sb - 1, "big"), (sb, "neg"), (nb - 1, "small")]
+            _cancel_blocks(w, ws, range(rows[0], rows[0] + 4), p1, g)
+            _cancel_blocks(w, ws, range(rows[1], rows[1] + 4), p2, g)
+        # down's big blocks read equal H blocks: gate / up rows copied
+        nb = inter // 32
+        for dst, src in ((nb // 4, nb // 4 - 1), (nb // 2, nb // 2 - 1)):
+            for base in (0, inter):
+                w13[base + 32 * dst : base + 32 * dst + 32] = w13[
+                    base + 32 * src : base + 32 * src + 32
+                ]
+                w13s[base + 32 * dst : base + 32 * dst + 32] = w13s[
+                    base + 32 * src : base + 32 * src + 32
+                ]
+        # down rows 8 .. 11 read the crafted gate rows' columns (H block 0) only
+        w2[8:12, 16:] = 0
+        return w13, w13s, w2, w2s
+

+        act = SiluAndMul()

+def _gdn_weights(g, K):
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.layernorm import RMSNormGated
+
+    w = {
+        "ln_w": _rnd(g, K.HIDDEN, scale=0.1),
+        "conv_w": _rnd(g, K.CONV, 1, K.CONV_W, scale=0.4),
+        "a_log": _rnd(g, K.NV, scale=0.5, dtype=torch.float32),
+        "dt_bias": _rnd(g, K.NV, scale=0.5),
+        "norm_w": (1 + _rnd(g, K.HD, scale=0.1, dtype=torch.float32)).to(BF),
+    }
+    w["w_qkvz"], w["w_qkvzs"] = _mxfp4(g, K.QKVZ, K.HIDDEN)
+    w["w_ba"], w["w_bas"] = _mxfp4(g, K.BA, K.HIDDEN)
+    w["w_o"], w["w_os"] = _mxfp4(g, K.HIDDEN, K.VAL)
+    gn = RMSNormGated(
+        K.HD, eps=EPS, group_size=None, norm_before_gate=True, dtype=BF
+    ).cuda()
+    gn.weight.data.copy_(w["norm_w"])
+    w["gated_norm"] = gn
+    return w
+

+def _rank_slice(K, w, tp, rank):
+    """The rank's column-parallel share of a GDN layer: each of q | k | v | z,
+    b | a, the conv's q | k | v and the heads' A_log / dt_bias cut in tp."""
+    if tp == 1:
+        return w
+    geo = K.Geo(tp)
+
+    def rows(t, parts):
+        return torch.cat(
+            [t[o + rank * n : o + (rank + 1) * n] for o, n in parts]
+        ).contiguous()
+
+    qkvz = [(0, geo.key), (K.KEY, geo.key), (2 * K.KEY, geo.val), (K.CONV, geo.val)]
+    heads = slice(rank * geo.nv, (rank + 1) * geo.nv)
+    out = dict(w)
+    out["w_qkvz"] = rows(w["w_qkvz"], qkvz)
+    out["w_qkvzs"] = rows(w["w_qkvzs"], qkvz)
+    out["w_ba"] = rows(w["w_ba"], [(0, geo.nv), (K.NV, geo.nv)])
+    out["w_bas"] = rows(w["w_bas"], [(0, geo.nv), (K.NV, geo.nv)])
+    out["conv_w"] = rows(w["conv_w"], qkvz[:3])
+    out["a_log"] = w["a_log"][heads].contiguous()
+    out["dt_bias"] = w["dt_bias"][heads].contiguous()
+    out["w_o"], out["w_os"] = _k_cols(w["w_o"], w["w_os"], K.VAL, tp, rank)
+    return out
+

+def _stock_gdn(K, geo, w, h, residual, conv, ssm, idx):
+    """The rank's heads (``geo``) -> core, residual out; ``conv`` / ``ssm``
+    updated in place."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops.causal_conv1d import causal_conv1d_update
+    from vllm.third_party.flash_linear_attention.ops import (
+        fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode,
+    )
+
+    x, res = _gemma_norm(h, residual, w["ln_w"])
+    qkvz = _linear(x, w["w_qkvz"], w["w_qkvzs"])
+    ba = _linear(x, w["w_ba"], w["w_bas"])
+    q, k, v, z = qkvz.split([geo.key, geo.key, geo.val, geo.val], dim=-1)
+    b, a = ba.split([geo.nv, geo.nv], dim=-1)
+    mixed = causal_conv1d_update(
+        torch.cat([q, k, v], dim=-1),
+        conv,
+        w["conv_w"].view(geo.conv, K.CONV_W),
+        None,
+        "silu",
+        conv_state_indices=idx,
+        null_block_id=-1,
+    )
+    o = torch.empty(h.size(0), 1, geo.nv, K.HD, dtype=BF, device="cuda")
+    fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode(
+        mixed_qkv=mixed,
+        a=a.contiguous(),
+        b=b.contiguous(),
+        A_log=w["a_log"],
+        dt_bias=w["dt_bias"],
+        scale=K.HD**-0.5,
+        initial_state=ssm,
+        out=o,
+        ssm_state_indices=idx,
+        use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
+    )
+    core = w["gated_norm"](o.view(-1, K.HD), z.reshape(-1, K.HD))
+    return core.view(h.size(0), geo.val), res
+

+"""The Qwen3.8-27B dense mono grid and stage plans, on the CPU.
+
+``tiling`` picks the grid from the device's compute units (256 on MI355X /
+MI350X, 128 on MI350P) and derives each K1 / K2 stage's per-CTA work from it.
+These tests need no GPU, FlyDSL or torch: the device query is replaced, and the
+kernels' task placement is replayed here in plain integers from the same plan
+(the formulas of ``dense_ffn`` / ``dense_gdn``), to check that every task runs
+exactly once at every validated width, that the 256-CTA plan is the one the
+kernels were written for, and that no GDN pass waits on a later one.
+"""

+from collections import Counter

+import pytest

+from vllm.models.qwen3_5.amd.mono import tiling as T

+GRIDS = T.VALIDATED_GRIDS

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the grid
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cus", [256, 128])
+def test_grid_is_a_validated_cu_count(cus):
+    assert T.resolve_grid(cus) == cus

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cus", [304, 240, 192, 160, 80, 64, 32])
+def test_unvalidated_cu_count_is_refused(cus):

+def test_override_runs_a_narrower_validated_grid():

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 256: as written

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- coverage
+def _once(counter, universe):
+    assert set(counter) == set(universe), "a task is never run"
+    assert all(n == 1 for n in counter.values()), "a task runs twice"

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("grid", GRIDS)
+def test_owners_cover_160_tasks_once(grid):
+    """o_proj / out_proj / K1 front: CTA b runs owners b + p grid < 160."""
+    got = Counter(
+        b + p * grid

+        for p in range(T.owner_passes(grid))
+        if b + p * grid < T.O_TASKS

+    _once(got, range(T.O_TASKS))

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tp", T.TP_SIZES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("grid", GRIDS)
+def test_gate_up_columns_once(grid, tp):
+    """K2 gate_up: CTA b's whole groups g_full b + j, then columns sl_off ..
+    sl_off + sl_cols of split group g_full grid + b / (16 / sl_cols)."""
+    geo = T.FGeo(tp, grid)
+    got = Counter()
+    for b in range(grid):
+        for j in range(geo.g_full):
+            g = geo.g_full * b + j
+            got.update((g, col) for col in range(T.ROWS))
+        per = T.ROWS // geo.sl_cols
+        g = geo.g_full * grid + b // per
+        off = b % per * geo.sl_cols
+        got.update((g, col) for col in range(off, off + geo.sl_cols))
+    _once(got, [(g, col) for g in range(geo.ng) for col in range(T.ROWS)])
+    # HQ: pairs of whole groups (j odd) are qdq blocks (g - 1) * 16 / 32
+    blocks = Counter(
+        (geo.g_full * b + j - 1) * T.ROWS // 32
+        for b in range(grid)
+        for j in range(1, geo.g_full, 2)
+    )
+    _once(blocks, range(geo.bulk_blocks))

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tp", T.TP_SIZES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("grid", GRIDS)
+def test_down_rows_once(grid, tp):
+    """K2 down: pass p's tiles on the even / odd waves (``d_pass_tiles``),
+    whole group i grid + b or the CTA's rows of the split group; the output
+    threads write exactly those rows (``down_out`` / ``down_out_split``)."""
+    geo = T.FGeo(tp, grid)
+    loaded, written = Counter(), Counter()
+    per = T.ROWS // geo.d_sl_rows
+    for b in range(grid):
+        for p in range(geo.d_passes):

+                    base = (geo.d_full + b // per) * T.ROWS
+                    rows = range(base + off, base + off + geo.d_sl_rows)
+                loaded.update(rows)
+                written.update(rows)
+    _once(loaded, range(T.HIDDEN))
+    _once(written, range(T.HIDDEN))

+def _task_of(geo, s, b, k):
+    """``dense_gdn.task_of`` in integers: (token, value head, chunk) or None
+    for a dead task."""
+    if geo.tpt % geo.grid == 0:
+        tpc = geo.tpt // geo.grid
+        w = (k % tpc) * geo.grid + b
+        return k // tpc, w // T.NVCH, w % T.NVCH
+    g = k * geo.grid + b
+    if g >= geo.tpt * s:
+        return None
+    w = g % geo.tpt
+    return g // geo.tpt, w // T.NVCH, w % T.NVCH

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
